sentences.text: South Australia’s Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence was asked how the state could improve its systems to prevent and respond to violence and support recovery and healing.

cites.document: With courage: South Australia’s vision beyond violence. Report of the Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence

sentences.text: The inquiry examined the extent of violence, its gendered drivers and risk factors, and how funding, service structures and coordination could change.

cites.document: With courage: South Australia’s vision beyond violence. Report of the Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence

sentences.text: The Commission concluded that the system was underfunded and fragmented, with crisis responses receiving more attention than prevention and early intervention.

cites.document: With courage: South Australia’s vision beyond violence. Report of the Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence

sentences.text: It also identified gaps in services for children and limited capacity to assess victim-survivors’ longer-term recovery needs.

items.quote: Despite decades of reform, the system remains underfunded, fragmented and reactive – driven more by crisis response than by prevention and early intervention.

cite.document: With courage: South Australia’s vision beyond violence. Report of the Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence

items.quote: South Australia does not have a statewide risk assessment and management framework.

cite.document: With courage: South Australia’s vision beyond violence. Report of the Royal Commission into Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence

items.quote: Services for children who have experienced domestic, family and sexual violence are almost non-existent.

items.quote: There is almost no capacity within the current system to work with victim-survivors to identify their medium- to longer-term needs.
